content.text:
Refactor Phase Complete. 26 passing, tsc clean.

## What changed

`/home/experimenter/experiments/runs/2026-09-04_06-20-44_claim-office-example-mapping_v6.1.1-lab-split-cc_opus-5-no-thinking-2/src/claim-office.ts`

**Naming evaluation (Rule 2 — done first).** The premium side already names its threshold check (`isHighlyEnchanted`); the claim side did not — the `>= 8` comparison was an inline expression inside `reimbursementRateFor`. Extracted `isHeavilyEnchanted(item)`. This restores symmetry with the premium side while keeping the two rules verbally distinct ("highly" = premium/5, "heavily" = claim/8), so the two-threshold separation stays visible in the names rather than only in the constants. Semantics untouched: still `>= REIMBURSEMENT_ENCHANTMENT_THRESHOLD`.

`reimbursementRateFor` now reads as a one-line rule selection:

```ts
const reimbursementRateFor = (item: Item): number =>
  isHeavilyEnchanted(item)
    ? HIGH_ENCHANTMENT_REIMBURSEMENT_RATE
    : FULL_REIMBURSEMENT_RATE;
```

**Rule 4 — `payoutForDamage(policy, damage)`.** The signature was `(damage, item)` and every call site had to resolve the item first, so `settleClaim`'s reducer carried the lookup plus a reversed argument order against its own `(policy, damages)` shape. Folding `damagedItem` into `payoutForDamage` removes one element from the reducer and makes the argument order consistent across `settleClaim` / `payoutForDamage` / `damagedItem`. `damagedItem` moved above its new caller; the non-null assertion is untouched.

## APP mass

Claim-payout cluster (`reimbursementRateFor`, `payoutForDamage`, `damagedItem`, `settleClaim` reducer):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| constants | 1 | 1 |
| bindings | 12 | 13 |
| invocations | 6 (12) | 6 (12) |
| conditionals | 1 (4) | 1 (4) |
| loops | 2 (10) | 2 (10) |
| **total** | **39** | **40** |

Mass rose by 1 — the extracted predicate adds a binding. Rule 2 trumps APP here: the cost buys a named claim-side threshold check matching the premium side's, and the delta is a single binding.

## Deliberately not done

Left alone per constraints: `intoAlikeGroups`, both non-null assertions, all threshold comparisons, the summed (not compounded) premium modifiers. Did not shape `reimbursementRateFor` for the upcoming dragon-material clause — the precedence order between full-reimbursement and the 50% rule isn't pinned down until the "50% rule wins" test exists, and guessing at it now would be implementing ahead. The current single-conditional form is a clean seam for that test to drive.
